name: Speechmatics

hlido_opinion.headline: Speech-to-text API platform with batch, real-time and voice-agent transcription, deployable in the cloud, on-prem or on-device.
hlido_opinion.body: Speechmatics is a developer-facing speech platform. Its public documentation covers a REST API for batch transcription of files, a WebSocket API for real-time transcription, an Agent STT mode that returns speaker-labelled turns for voice agents, and text to speech. Official SDKs are listed for Python, JavaScript, .NET and Rust, with integrations for LiveKit, Pipecat and Vapi. Batch jobs can call back to a URL you control when they finish. The service runs as a managed cloud API, as on-prem containers or Kubernetes, and on-device on Mac and Windows. Dedicated medical models are documented. Hlido's review covers the public surface only: we did not benchmark transcription accuracy or run the APIs, so this score reflects how clearly the product, pricing, documentation and security claims are presented. Correction, 2026-11-20: an earlier version of this page said Speechmatics offered no API, SDK or webhooks and was not suited to real-time or specialised use. That was wrong. After a correction request from the vendor we checked each point against the public documentation and rewrote the text. The overall score is unchanged.

tier_rationale: STEADY (78) because the public surface is clear: the value proposition, a pricing link, documentation and security claims were all found without a login. Not VITAL because this is a public-surface review at medium confidence: Hlido did not test transcription accuracy or API behaviour hands-on.
what_it_does_well: Documents both a REST batch API and a WebSocket real-time API, with a public API reference
Lists official SDKs for Python, JavaScript, .NET and Rust, plus LiveKit, Pipecat and Vapi integrations
Offers three deployment routes: managed cloud, on-prem containers or Kubernetes, and on-device on Mac and Windows
Publishes dedicated medical models and a language list covering 55+ languages
what_it_fails_at: On-device deployment is by access request, with pricing through sales rather than a public price
The newer multilingual models (Melia 1, Oak 1) do not yet support custom dictionary or confidence scores, per the vendor's model table
Some features are cloud-only, including summarization, auto chapters, topic detection and Agent STT
We did not find an official MCP server in the public documentation, and the legacy Python CLI is deprecated
best_for: Developers adding batch or real-time transcription to a product through an API
Teams building voice agents that need speaker-labelled, turn-based transcripts
Organisations that must keep audio in their own environment, on-prem or on-device
Healthcare transcription projects that need a medical-vocabulary model
not_recommended_for: Buyers who need independently verified accuracy figures: this review did not benchmark transcription quality
Teams that want self-serve, publicly priced on-device deployment
Multilingual projects that need custom dictionary or confidence scores on the Melia 1 or Oak 1 models today

compared_to.verdict_diff: Both offer real-time streaming and batch transcription through an API. Speechmatics also documents on-prem containers and on-device deployment; Google Cloud Speech-to-Text fits teams already building on Google Cloud.

Rev provides human transcription services alongside automated options, making it a better choice for users needing high accuracy in specific contexts. Speechmatics is better for automated, high-volume needs.

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: REST API for batch jobs and WebSocket APIs for real-time and Agent STT, with official SDKs for Python, JavaScript, .NET and Rust. Batch jobs can notify a callback URL on completion. An API key is required. No official MCP server was found in the public documentation.

checklist.evidence: Transparent pricing available on the website

summary: Speech-to-text API platform with batch, real-time and voice-agent transcription, deployable in the cloud, on-prem or on-device.
